$comment: Machine-readable rename map for the noy-db 0.7.0-pre vocabulary change — the port-instance naming rule. A type a satellite IMPLEMENTS is now `Noydb<Stem>`, matching `NoydbStore`, which was already the pattern and is unchanged (689 references across five repos; the scheme accommodates the anchor rather than renaming it). The `Provider` suffix is retired: it marked some port instances and not others, so it distinguished nothing. Every `from` was REMOVED with no alias, per the project's no-legacy-aliases policy — `/kernel` and `/adapter` were both retired that way after consumers migrated. Rows are verified against the live surface by packages/hub/__tests__/codemod-map-0.7.test.ts. ABSENT BY MEASUREMENT, not by oversight: StoreCoordinationProvider and createDefaultCoordinationProvider were renamed in the same sweep but are reachable from NO declared subpath of the published 0.6.0 tarball, so no consumer could hold them — the same reason SubsystemBus is absent from the 0.6 map. Listing them would repeat #1052's over-count.

renames.note: The `at-*` port instance. Published from the root barrel AND @noy-db/hub/cargo in 0.6.0; both keep re-exporting it under the new name.
The in-memory double an at-* implementor tests against. Follows its interface rather than keeping a suffix the interface no longer has.

The `by-*` port instance: who is live, and what generation are they on. Named for the participants rather than the wire — `PeerChannel` is the transport, and a mesh has no head, which the previous name's alternatives (Coordinator, Conductor) implied. Published from @noy-db/hub/cargo in 0.6.0; /cargo keeps re-exporting it under the new name.
Sibling of NoydbSealer for device-bound sealing. Published from the root barrel and @noy-db/hub/team.
